historical_context.time_period: Industrial Greathold, after mixed-metal runic craft and rail service have become ordinary workshop practice
historical_context.location: Coppervein Repairs, a fixture-local public-facing rune shop beneath the terrace rail stair by Cistern House Nine's street landing in the unnamed warm-sea Hold.
historical_context.summary: An apprentice receives a rail conductor's warming inspection lamp and discovers that its accepted colour slip was cut for the old pale-stone face rather than the current dark-slate replacement.

public_facts.text: A colour slip is a thumb-length, null-terminated witness cut on matching substrate with the proposed channel materials and a job mark; it proves one small seam under one small working rather than certifying a whole graph.
Pump and rail crews commonly return an accepted colour slip with the object, and same slip means matching substrate, channel sequence, and fill as well as the visible rune.
Market rainbow is Greathold shop slang for coloured seams whose prestige may exceed their function; the phrase may praise a showpiece or accuse its maker of unnecessary expense.
Gold-filled channels carry many patterns with little interference, while substrate, material, junction, depth, and prior flow history can change what an otherwise familiar graph does.

ambient_pressures.text: Fresh witness work consumes a matching offcut, trace fills, a crystal shaving, and bench time that can compete with a rail departure.
A workshop gains trust from repaired tools and remembered materials, but attractive old proof can become sales pressure when the current material has changed.
An apprentice can inspect, test, quote, request instruction, and refuse a completion step; Mastership and the workshop's civic standing remain separate from one job's bench choices.

groups.label: Coppervein Repairs
institutional_logic: Turn material knowledge into repairs whose costs and limits can travel with the object.
Train apprentices on small witnessed failures before letting a whole graph carry the lesson.
material_incentives: Finish work before customer schedules expire.
Avoid wasting precious fill or attaching the workshop mark to stale proof.
internal_virtues: A returned slip with its job mark intact
internal_shames: Passing an old witness as current
Letting a repair return with the same fault
prestige_markers: A repair that misses notice in ordinary use
A failure caught on scrap rather than finished work
taboo_triggers: Treating a whole graph as proved by one attractive seam
emotional_display_norms: Concern appears as object comparison, dry correction, material arithmetic, and who is allowed to hold the workshop punch.
trust_defaults: Trusts matched witnesses, observed heat, named material cost, and customers who return the old slip with the object.
speech_register_cues: Same slip and market rainbow slang

groups.label: Terrace rail crews
institutional_logic: Keep ordinary rail tools working across scheduled departures.
Return service witnesses when a repair needs to be repeated or challenged.
material_incentives: Keep repair bills, spare-tool inconvenience, and repeat faults small.
internal_virtues: A tool returned with its service witness
A complaint that names when and where the fault appears
A departure met with usable equipment
internal_shames: Missing a train over counter vanity
Paying twice for the same warming handle
prestige_markers: A full shift with borrowed tools returned
Knowing which repair shop remembers the job
taboo_triggers: A shop treating schedule pressure as permission to reuse irrelevant proof
A purchasing office mistaking low price for solved work
emotional_display_norms: Impatience appears as bell counting, glove complaints, invoice jokes, and one hand kept on the object at the counter.
trust_defaults: Trusts a cool handle, a clear price, and a returned witness more than a beautiful channel alone.

cultural_pressure_fields.summary: A colour slip gains value by staying narrow: one matched seam, one small working, one attached job.
cultural_pressure_fields.projection_use: Make bench choices exchange time, material, and customer patience for evidence about the current object rather than generic certainty.

cultural_pressure_fields.summary: A small fault competes with a real departure, while the wrong quick repair sends the same object back through the counter later.
cultural_pressure_fields.projection_use: Show rail pressure through bells, gloves, spare tools, and the object's return rather than escalating the scene into public danger.

observer_read: Customers who think a timetable can settle a material question
Repeat business whose returned objects carry useful evidence
target_self_read: Workers paying for shop delay with missed duties and bad spare tools
Competent users who know how the fault appears in service
misread_patterns: The bench may dismiss the conductor's heat report as impatience.
Craft pride may hide the cost of a missed departure.
factional_misread_matrix.projection_use: Let customer observation narrow the fault while the workshop retains responsibility for the material inference.

observer_read: Skilled people who can turn a warm handle into a day of expensive stone scraps
The shop whose punch decides whether the current job has a witness
target_self_read: Workers containing uncertainty before it reaches the finished graph
A teaching practice carried through customer work
misread_patterns: A bright old slip may look more convincing than a new stained one.
A refusal to punch may look like rank protecting itself.
factional_misread_matrix.projection_use: Keep trust split among visible evidence, time, price, and workshop behavior rather than letting one speech settle it.

role_pressure_fields.summary: A developing craftsperson trusted with customer intake and bench tests while working beneath a Master's workshop mark.
obligations: Match the witness to the current material
Name the cost of time and fill
Ask for instruction when inference outruns training
Avoid certifying more than the test shows
failure_modes: Trusting an accepted but mismatched slip
Making a correct refusal nobody else can understand

role_pressure_fields.summary: A practiced tool user who knows when the lamp warms, owns the departure problem, and can accept cost or delay after seeing the evidence.
obligations: Return the lamp and its service witness
Report the fault as it appears in use
Carry the repair choice back to the rail office
failure_modes: Buying the quick copy from weak proof
Treating craft time as personal obstruction
Letting purchasing choose colour over use

known_context.text: Kela knows the shop's colour-slip practice, reachable bench tools, current object surfaces, customer statements, and the tests she personally performs.

beliefs.text: Kela believes an accepted witness keeps its value only while it matches the material work it witnessed.

misreads.text: Kela may treat a customer's departure pressure as vanity before recognizing the cost of missed work.

must_not_know.text: Kela cannot infer the behavior of the entire lamp graph from one witness junction or generalize this local copper-and-slate failure to every material pairing.

known_context.text: Ovra knows workshop practice, mixed-material risks, apprentice instruction, and what the workshop punch admits about a completed job.

beliefs.text: Ovra believes a narrow failed witness is more useful than a broad attractive claim.

misreads.text: Ovra may use silence as instruction after the customer needs an explicit account of delay or cost.

must_not_know.text: Ovra cannot make an untested graph safe by applying a mark or claim universal material law from this repair.

known_context.text: Senn knows the lamp's service history, when and where its handle warms, the returned slip, the depot spare, the repair price, and the train schedule.

beliefs.text: Senn believes a useful repair should survive normal gloved work and arrive before the duty that needs it.

misreads.text: Senn may mistake the old slip's accepted mark and bright seams for proof about the replacement stone.

must_not_know.text: Senn cannot know which seam causes the heat until observed bench evidence narrows it.

author_only_boundaries.text: Coppervein Repairs, Kela, Ovra, Senn, and this lamp repair are fixture-local generated elaboration. The durable colour-slip practice lives in the authored section of Runic Engineering; the scene is not canonical history merely because it uses it.
The local dark-slate, copper, depth, and heat relation illustrates a single repair. It does not define a universal rune-material table or a Greathold standard.

open_questions.question: Which named Hold contains Cistern House Nine and Coppervein Repairs?
open_questions.notes: The canonical warm-sea Hold remains unnamed. The fixture adds a shop near the existing street landing without naming the Hold.

open_questions.question: Do major rail offices maintain a formal colour-slip standard or only accept local workshop customs?
open_questions.notes: The fixture uses the authored common custom and one local workshop punch. It does not establish a Greathold-wide standards body.

open_questions.question: Which substrate and channel-fill pairings recur often enough to deserve an authored technical catalogue?
open_questions.notes: The source intentionally leaves quantitative material semantics open. This fixture should not harden its one repair into the catalogue.
